question: What percentage (0-100) of revenue comes from unique customers who have more than one delivered order?
sql:
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        o.order_id,
        o.customer_id,
        c.customer_unique_id,
        (oi.price + oi.freight_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
),
customer_order_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_unique_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS delivered_order_cnt
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY customer_unique_id
),
revenue_by_customer AS (
    SELECT 
        d.customer_unique_id,
        SUM(d.revenue) AS customer_revenue,
        coc.delivered_order_cnt
    FROM delivered_orders d
    JOIN customer_order_counts coc
        ON d.customer_unique_id = coc.customer_unique_id
    GROUP BY d.customer_unique_id, coc.delivered_order_cnt
),
total_rev AS (
    SELECT SUM(customer_revenue) AS total_revenue FROM revenue_by_customer
),
multi_rev AS (
    SELECT SUM(customer_revenue) AS multi_revenue
    FROM revenue_by_customer
    WHERE delivered_order_cnt > 1
)
SELECT 
    (multi_rev.multi_revenue / total_rev.total_revenue) * 100.0 AS revenue_percentage_from_multi_order_customers
FROM total_rev, multi_rev
